description.narrative: Niger, Malaria, Catholic Relief Services - United States Conference of Catholic Bishops (CRS Niger)This program has the following goals: By 2018, reduce malaria incidence by 75 percent compared to 2013. By 2018, reduce malaria mortality by 75 percent compared to 2013. The objectives of this program are: At least 80 percent of children aged 3-59 months in target areas for seasonal malaria chemoprevention received adequate protection during the last high transmission period (at least three treatments). At least 80 percent of malaria epidemics in at-risk health districts are detected within two weeks of starting and receive an appropriate response. At least 80 percent of pregnant women received IPT3 during their last pregnancy. At least 80 percent of the population at risk of malaria uses LLINs, especially children aged under 1 year and pregnant women. At least 80 percent of the population is familiar with the key signs of malaria and with national preventive measures. At least 90 percent of confirmed malaria cases received appropriate antimalarial treatment in accordance with national guidelines. At least 90 percent of suspected malaria cases seen in outpatient clinics at health care facilities and in the community (by outreach workers) received a parasitological test (microscopy or RDT) in accordance with national guidelines
